facts: One metal chamber is shown in oblique cutaway, with an exposed internal compartment to the right and a tall curved polished front face to the left.
The curved front face has one C-shaped printed label. Its narrow right cut edge is hatched; that tall edge is not an extra air outlet.
The chamber has a sloping upper edge, right wall and lower edge. K is printed beneath the chamber.
No separate support stand, valve, pump switch or numerical chamber dimensions are shown.
The lower part of the cutaway compartment contains liquid, indicated by a surface and horizontal marks; the current lesson identifies it as ether.
A single upright thermometer enters through the top, left of the immersed bent tube.
The thermometer has a rounded upper end, a narrow stem with fine dark graduations and a dark lower bulb. No legible numeric thermometer reading is printed.
In the drawing, the thermometer's lower tip is above the depicted liquid surface. Do not silently move it into the liquid.
The letter-like mark in the liquid resembles Cyrillic Э or a handwritten 3; its material role follows the lesson's ether identification, not a numerical value.
Dark stippling and hatching at the upper chamber are cutaway/shading marks, not a measured particle count or a required new flow arrow.
One continuous external hose runs from the top-right chamber port upward around a large loop, then bends down/right to the pump assembly at lower right.
The chamber-side tube continues from that port down the right side of the compartment, bends inward and ends below the liquid surface.
The external pump assembly has two connected rounded lobes, one higher/right with heavy texture and one lower/left with a rounded pear-like contour.
The original apparatus-label glyph Г is beside the pump. The authorized modern apparatus notation is Latin G.
The source has no process-direction arrows, pressure readings, operating sequence or quantitative flow labels.
